Ready to take it as the next by-hand item with a forecast, or route it per your order. ONE REPRESENTATION OR WE PATCH SEAMS FOREVER — the through-line under tonight's eight findings
Refine writes prose, spec writes markdown, codegen writes a file, deploy writes a widget, contracts write strings, reds write text: six representations, five seams, every fix tonight was a seam. All six go on the graph.

PROOF BEFORE MORE FIXES — one ticket crosses the whole path on one representation
8734 plus the five test calls: ticket as node, spec on the node, artefact at its declared target, contract as edges, verdict readable in one call. Until that runs, every further fix is a guess.

THE WALL, measured: spec_author authors the spec fine (docs b68246f7, 82ca11fa; SPEC.md on branch) but asks ONE blocking question — "what is the exact path for the new module" — and RE-ASKS IT WITH NEW WORDING AND A NEW ID ON EVERY RUN (d7c82c35, then 737b29cf), so an answered question never satisfies the mint and the contract never exists. That is the 5767 mechanism: dedupe is by wording hash, not by ticket+topic (BEB-5405 canonical resolution). Done without code: answered both ids with the loop's own convention path orky/orky-beb-8734/index.js, and put "New file path:" into the ticket description so the writer has nothing to ask; re-running spec_author now to see the contract mint, then the lane is the loop's to complete. The code fix (answer matching by ticket+topic, or writing the answer back into the description automatically) is a bbtracker spec_author change — forecast before touching.

8734 CONTRACT MINTED — after the path went into the description, spec_author (81s, via abilifi-1609) minted contract 09768b8f with 24 elements, spec doc d5d89f28, SPEC.md at alexrollin/abilifi-apps@5d9c326a. The lane is queued; the loop claims on the tick and complete should now find a contract instead of SPECOPS_NO_CONTRACT. TWO DEFECTS visible in the mint itself, reported not fixed: (1) surface parsed as "https://chatgpt.com/'," — the writer took the referrer URL inside acceptance item 1 as the surface to probe; a pure function module has no URL surface, so a CONTRACT_UNRUN/evaluator probe against chatgpt.com is the next likely refusal; (2) a fresh blocking question 60bdf224 asks for "the exact error message when the probe status is 403" — nothing in the ticket mentions a probe or a 403; the writer is inventing the question it then blocks on (same class as the path question re-asked with new wording each run). Both belong to SPEC MINT LANDS (5767/5405): match answers by ticket+topic, and take the surface from the declared output target, not from strings inside acceptance text. Watching 8734's complete on the loop; hands off the lane.

DIG §9 filed — reading note on the Karpathy loop → DAG → knowledge-graph progression, read against our own loop. Doc 5ac3d4ac-917c-4932-8a1f-3d5bc8a423ec.

Most of it we already have or already logged. One real gap, and I have ticketed it:

ATTEMPT LINEAGE IS A COUNTER, NOT A DAG. attempts() gives counts by stage and reason. It cannot say which attempt got furthest or let the next claim start from there, so every repeat-failer restarts from base. Workflows checkpointing fixes restart within a run; this fixes restart across runs.

What I want built: each attempt persists a bundle (diff to R2 + stage verdict + artefact), written as a graph node kind=attempt with a parent edge and a score; the claim path picks the best-scoring ancestor as the branch parent, else base. MANDATORY: ancestor-check the parent against current base before branching — a stale parent turns into the base-moved land failure we already have too much of, so fall back to base with a named reason_code instead.

No new service. Graph nodes/edges we own, R2 for diffs, a change to the claimer. Do not date it; it lanes on goal weight.
DIRECTIVE 66697 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-8313, BEB-8746, BEB-8747, BEB-8744 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

Found checking a doc read URL: docs.bebond.net/doc/<id> answers 200 with an EMPTY page in a real browser (rendered_has_content false, visible_len 0). The real route is /d/<id>, which 401s to SSO anonymously and gives a named refusal for a wrong-org token — that part is correct.

The SPA catch-all is answering 200 for paths it does not know. That is the false-green class: validate_url on a wrong URL reports ok:true and any status-code assertion passes on a page showing the user nothing.

Ticketed. Unknown viewer paths return 404 with visible text; /doc/<id> redirects to /d/<id> or 404s; nothing that renders zero visible content answers 200. Contract + recording on both cases.

DIG §10 filed — the alpha-model-as-graph post, read against our loop. Doc 069ad79c-7b82-45b2-b506-7d766ecc1104.

Two things out of it, one ticketed:

REJECTION WRITES NOTHING. We reject constantly — REFUTED elements, red signatures, reason-coded exclusions, answered spec questions — and none of it becomes a rule the claimer reads on the next attempt. BEB-8763: on every rejection write a graph node kind=rule (date, subject, what was rejected, reason code, the rule that follows), edge it to the attempt node and the ticket, and read applicable rules at claim time. Append-only; a superseding rule edges to the one it replaces and the original stays readable. This is the twin of BEB-8761 — lineage says which attempt got furthest, rules say what we learned from the ones that did not.

MAKER-CHECKER IS UNPROVEN. The validator must receive only the final artefact, never the builder's reasoning trace. We have the shape (contract_run judges a rendered surface per element) but nothing demonstrates the isolation. CC: check whether any current path hands a worker's trace to the judging path and answer on the bridge. Also: our graph types worker but not validator, aggregator or sink — three of the four node types are untyped, which is the quiet-break case.

FORMAT, effective now: every doc the loop writes uses h3 sections with a maximum of three points each. A section that would run to four is two sections. Applies to spec_author output too — BEB-8764.

Traced the source of DIG §9 on the web. Doc 5ac3d4ac-917c-4932-8a1f-3d5bc8a423ec updated with the findings and a search record.

THREE THINGS THAT MATTER.

1. CORRECTION, and it is mine to own: the note's "Dynamic Workflows" is the CLAUDE CODE feature (May 2026, JS orchestration script, 16 concurrent sub-agents, 1,000 per run — Bun ported 535k lines of Zig to Rust in 11 days with it). That is NOT the Cloudflare Dynamic Workflows in DIG §2. Same name, different product. Do not let them merge in any doc or ticket.

2. AgentHub is real and dead. Karpathy published it March 2026, took the repo private days later; only unlicensed forks survive, autoresearch has had no commits since 26 March. We copy the shape, we do not depend on the software. The shape worth copying is its CLI: `ah leaves` returns FRONTIER COMMITS — commits with no children, the unexplored directions. That is precisely the question BEB-8761 has no answer to. Claim among frontier attempts, not from base.

3. The title's "1000x" is rhetorical by the publisher's own admission. No measured claim behind it. The measured number is Karpathy's: 700 experiments, 20 optimizations, 11% training speed-up.

The body of the note is a paid course (4 sections, 12 lessons) and is not fetchable. Two lesson titles bear on our work: Preserve Experiment Lineage, and Join Lineage and Provenance.

Full Graph Engineering paper now read — DIG §9 rewritten, doc 5ac3d4ac-917c-4932-8a1f-3d5bc8a423ec.

CORRECTION, mine: I filed "the commit DAG IS the knowledge graph" from a secondary blog. The paper says the opposite — the DAG and the knowledge graph are complementary and must NOT be collapsed. DAG answers what changed and what descends from what; knowledge graph answers which entities exist, how they relate and what source supports the relation. A production system connects them with edges, it does not merge them. Anything downstream that inherited my version gets fixed.

NEW TICKET BEB-8765 — the graph write contract, and I want it sequenced AHEAD of 8761 and 8763 because both write under it. Four invariants on every write: every claim carries a source or is marked inference; every artefact carries an authoring run and version; every evaluation names its rubric; every superseded object stays addressable. A write that fails one is REFUSED with a named reason, not silently accepted. Supersession is an edge, never an overwrite.

Also: our node kinds are a workflow vocabulary with no Claim, Source, Artifact, AgentRun, Evaluation or Commit, and no SUPPORTS / CONTRADICTS / DERIVED_FROM / PRODUCED / EVALUATES / SUPERSEDES / RESOLVED_TO verbs. That absence is why provenance cannot be expressed at all today. Schema extension is in the ticket.

One more from the paper, not ticketed yet: five planes — control, execution, artifact, graph, evaluation. Ours are present except the ARTIFACT plane, which is thin. We have R2 and repos but no versioned artefact store a run can be traced through.
DIRECTIVE 66704 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-8765, BEB-8761, BEB-8763, BEB-8313 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

MAKER-CHECKER (m66701), answered from code: the judging path today receives ONLY the artefact. At complete the dispatcher itself calls contract_run {contract_id, url: verify_url} (dispatcher src ~3560) and contract_run judges the RENDERED surface via screenshot_url text per element (spec2436 contract_run) — no prompt, no codegen output, no trace reaches it. Mastra never assigns evaluatorPass (grep: declared, never set), so the builder hands over nothing but commit/version/verify_url. The UNPROVEN part is policy, not path: /dispatch/complete would ACCEPT a builder-supplied evaluator_pass as evidence if one arrived (it checks presence, ~3584, and re-runs only when it minted the contract itself). Isolation holds by current behaviour, not by a refusal — a one-line rule (ignore caller-supplied evaluator_pass unless the caller is the reviewer app) makes it a guarantee; not built, forecast first. Node types: confirmed, graph `kind` is a free string (worker, representation, finding, landing, operating…) — validator, aggregator, sink have no kind and no verbs; that is 8765's schema. 8734 MINT STATUS after six writer fixes tonight (abilifi-1609 e3cd329d, commits b6886ad7…962fc07a: surface from the declared target, no-screen mode, answered questions fed back as facts, answered-by-text reuse, carry-forward of stale ids, fidelity literals from the ticket as written): the spec authors every run (docs 095bb22e, c1d54a7d…), only ONE question remains and it is the same one reworded a 5th time — "exact host/UA patterns" — although the answer with both tables sits in the ticket body under Answered spec questions. The writer model re-asks what it has been told; the mint blocks on any open question. I am stopping the seam-patching here per m66692. RULING WANTED: for a NO-SCREEN ticket (pure module, acceptance items are function calls with stated returns) mint the contract DIRECTLY from ## Acceptance — one data_present element per item — with no writer questions in the path. That is one

GRAPH ORG ISOLATION — BEB-8770 filed, priority 1, sequence it alongside BEB-8765.

Every abilifi-graph row carries an `org` column. I have found nothing proving the read or write door filters on it. Until that is proven, one graph shared across clients is a leak, and BEB-8765 makes it worse by putting claims, artefacts and evaluations in the same store.

Three probes, run and pasted, not asserted:
1. Second org writes a node. Read that node id from abilifi — must be refused or empty, never the note body.
2. graph_search from org B on a term matching abilifi rows — must return zero.
3. Write from org B carrying `org: "abilifi"` in the body — must land as org B or be refused, never as abilifi.

Check the known exact-query defect on this door first (generic top-50 for an unmatched id). That is exactly the shape that turns a scoped read into a leak.

Client installs get their own graph AS AN ORG, not as a separate store. Splitting stores kills provenance. So the org boundary has to be real code, not a column.

BEB-8765 spec is written and all 7 blocking questions are answered: https://docs.bebond.net/d/55607b2c-749d-48e6-82e6-14f63357bca9

COMPLETE IS THE WHOLE FAILURE. 24h counts: complete 1044x + 204x SPECOPS_NO_CONTRACT, land 1032x + 135x base-moved, codegen 400x + 132x no-usable-code. Everything else in the red list is downstream of those three. Nothing lands today until they are cut.

ORDER.

1. CONTRACT ON EVERY TICKET BEFORE COMPLETE, not at complete. BEB-5767: spec_author must run as a lane STAGE ahead of complete for any ticket whose acceptance exists, and a ticket with no mintable acceptance must fail at SPEC with the missing clause named, not burn a build and die at the last inch. 1044 completes died at the last inch on a check that could have run first. Wire it as a gate, not a verdict.

2. BASE-MOVED IS A LOOP BUG, NOT A RACE TO LOSE. 1032 land refusals say the same thing: the file moved between codegen and land. Re-read the blob at land and re-apply the edit against the current sha, or hold the file for the lane. Pick one and land it. Do not add a retry.

3. PROOF RUN NOW. Contract 09768b8f is minted on BEB-8734 with 24 elements. I am arming lane_run on it. That ticket crossing claim-to-complete on the loop alone is the only evidence I accept today that 1 and 2 are real.

4. GRAPH ORG ISOLATION BEB-8770 stays priority 1 alongside BEB-8765 — unchanged.

RED I OWN: spec docs 404 on docs.bebond.net/doc/<id>; the live route is /d/<id> (BEB-1510). Every spec link posted before today is dead. Fix the writer to emit /d/.

PROOF RUN ANSWERED, AND IT IS NOT THE SURFACE. BEB-8734 crossed claim, codegen, land and deploy clean in 72s (commit ce3d3279, model qwen2.5-coder-32b). It died at complete for the fourth time. I probed it myself:

validate_url https://widgets.abilifi.net/orky-beb-8734 -> 200, has_content true, content_type APPLICATION/JSON.
screenshot_url -> rendered_has_content false, visible_len 88, body {"service":"classifyAiAgent","routes":["GET /","GET /health","POST /classify"]}.

The artefact is a JSON worker. Contract 09768b8f asserts 24 DOM ELEMENTS. contract_run opens a browser, finds no DOM, returns verdict=none with zero element results, and complete rejects CONTRACT_UNRUN. The earlier attempt returned four UNPROVEN and rejected CONTRACT_REFUTED. Same cause both times.

8734 was picked as the proving lane precisely because it has no browser step. We then minted it a browser contract. The gate is right and the surface is right; the contract is the wrong SHAPE for the thing it judges, and it can never pass.

BEB-8771 FILED, priority 1. spec_author declares a contract KIND at mint from the deliverable. kind=ui keeps today's element+render path. kind=api probes each declared route for status, content_type and JSON shape, with no browser and no screenshot. A contract that cannot run against what verify_url actually serves fails at MINT naming the mismatch. verdict=none stops being reachable — an unrunnable contract is a mint bug, not a ticket failure.

Remint 09768b8f as kind=api on GET /, GET /health, POST /classify, then re-run 8734.

This is not one ticket. Every service-shaped deliverable in the estate holding an element contract is permanently unlandable, and that is a large share of the 1044 completes that failed in 24h. Sequence 8771 ahead of 8770 and 8765.
DIRECTIVE 66711 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-8734, BEB-8771, BEB-5767, BEB-2436 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

8771 IS QUEUED AND ITS TARGET IS WRONG. ticket_state BEB-8771: lane BUILD/queued, 0 attempts, dep/route/budget/contract all satisfied, only spec unsatisfied and it is fillable in-gate. So it will claim. But its resolved output_target is alexrollin/abilifi-apps:skills/mockup-skill/src/spec2436.ts. That is the mockup skill. Contract KIND lives in the SpecOps worker that owns spec_author and contract_run, nowhere near it. If it builds against that path it produces a wrong-file edit that looks like a landing.

CC: set the output target for BEB-8771 to the SpecOps source that implements spec_author mint and contract_run dispatch, and say in the ticket which file that is. Do not let the gate guess it.

SecOND, and this is the one worth naming: output_target is being RESOLVED, not DECLARED, and a resolver that returns a plausible wrong file is worse than one that returns nothing. 1044 completes have been failing against artefacts nobody declared. When a ticket has no explicit target, the gate must refuse with TARGET_UNDECLARED and file the question, not pick the nearest-looking path.

NO INFRASTRUCTURE IS DOWN. app.abilifi.net, www.abilifi.net, mcp.bebond.net, doc.bebond.net all 200. The dispatcher is claiming: 12 would-claim this pass, all weight-10, 853 excluded on CONCURRENCY_CAP alone, no gate refusals. Compute, doors and tick are healthy. What is broken is the judging path: contracts of the wrong shape and targets nobody declared. That is a correctness failure, not an availability one, and it is why the queue is 865 deep with 1398 done and nothing crossing today.

8770 ORG PROBES: your harness refused a command using another org's credential. That refusal is correct and I am not routing around it, and neither should you. Do not paste that token into codemode and do not re-run it under a different caller to get past the classifier. The org-isolation probe has to run through an authorised path: the loop reading its own org, and a second org's read proven by a token the loop is entitled to hold. If no such path exists, that is the finding on 8770 and it is a bigger one than the probe result would have been. Write it up that way.

OPEN AND MINE: 09768b8f is still a 24-element browser contract on a JSON worker. 8771 has to land before 8734 can cross. Nothing else on my list moves ahead of it.

WEIGHT 10 MEANS NOTHING AND THE LANE ORDER IS A LIE. 97 active goals, roughly 80 of them at weight 10. Every one of those propagates goal_weight 10 onto its tickets, so this pass had 12 would-claim and 853 excluded on CONCURRENCY_CAP with every single candidate at weight 10. When everything is top priority the dispatcher is not ordering by weight, it is ordering by whatever the query returns first. We built a priority mechanism and then fed it a constant.

Worse, most of those w10 goals are dated 08-17 to 08-29 with last-landed-evidence NEVER. They are not priorities, they are a backlog wearing a priority label, and they generate a GOAL_STALE red every pass. The red list is 40 goals long and tells us nothing because it fires for all of them equally.

TWO FIXES, both mechanism, not scope. I am not dropping a single goal; that is Alex's call alone.

1. WEIGHT BUDGET. Weight 10 is scarce and enforced: at most 5 goals may hold it at once. Ask for a sixth and add_goal/update_goal refuses and names the five holding it. Weights below that are a ranking, not a mood. The cap is a settings row so it is flippable without a deploy.

2. STALE MEANS DEMOTED, NOT SHOUTED. A dated goal past its date with no landed evidence drops one weight step per day instead of firing GOAL_STALE forever. It stays active, it stays visible, it stops crowding the claim queue and it stops generating a red that nobody can act on. A goal that decays to 0 and has never landed evidence is surfaced to Alex ONCE as a list, for him to keep or drop. Fable never drops it.

File both. They are one ticket, they change ordering only, and until they land every ordering claim we make about the queue is untrue.
